subject: ventures/gutter-install-bid-calculator
professional: an owner-estimator at a small seamless-gutter install shop, who would check first that the bid covers crew-hours at a real crew size, material and overhead, and that price-per-foot lands near what local shops actually charge

evidence.correctness: Ran `node /tmp/.../chk.mjs` (calculateBid on three of the four shipped presets with the page's default rates) and recomputed each independently in a separate Python script from the formulas in the README (loaded wage = wage*(1+burden), overhead on direct cost, price = cost/(1-margin)). Preset 1 (140 ft ranch): 8.1 h, labor $406.30, material $524.00, cost $1,189.34, price $1,749.03, both agree. Preset 3 (220 ft 6in colonial): 32.26 h, cost $4,611.88, price $6,782.18, agree. Preset 4 (160 ft copper): 21.61 h, cost $5,029.94, price $7,396.97, agree, and the $7,396.97 quoted on the pricing page matches. Margin-on-price (not markup) is the standard method. Caveat: recompute uses the author's own method and rates; no external industry rate table was available through the proxy, so rates are unverified (see domain).
evidence.completeness: Checked each README feature: profile/story presets (work), included-drop and extra-footage logic (works, short runs clamp to 0), inside/outside miters, fascia, tear-off, steep access, hidden hangers, permit (all in calc.mjs and returned), walk-away price (breakEvenPrice = totalCost), proposed-price comparison (works), copy bid summary (formatBidSummary works). Also ships proposal.mjs, proposal-terms.mjs, share.mjs not mentioned in the README. Three comparison/guide pages exist and render their numbers. No TODO stubs found. README does not document proposal/share features.
evidence.verification: Ran `cd ventures/gutter-install-bid-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 122 tests, 122 pass, 0 fail. Seeded mutation 1 in calc.mjs (extra downspout footage allowance used includedDownspouts instead of downspouts): 2 tests failed (calc.test.mjs + proposal.test.mjs run, 57 pass 2 fail), reverted with git checkout. Seeded mutation 2 (overhead charged on labor only instead of direct cost): full suite 120 pass, 2 fail, caught, reverted. File confirmed clean by git status. Tests are good on arithmetic; the weakness is that no test compares to an externally sourced bid.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs in full (365 lines), skimmed test names. Pure, DOM-free, validated inputs with named errors, clean separation of hour and cost lines, divide-by-zero guarded, margin >=100 rejected. Defects: `flag()` falls through to Boolean() for arbitrary strings (so 'no' is true); presets duplicate the included-drop constants in every preset; per-line hour/rate defaults live in index.html and are not exported from calc.mjs, so page defaults and suggestedProfileKit can drift. Not a copied engine; minor.
evidence.claims: Checked: README live URL marisstella.app matches VENTURE.yaml production link (ok); disclaimer present in README and page (ok); page numbers ($7,396.97, $46.23/ft, 21.6 h) match computed output (ok); usage events and localStorage key match usage.mjs (ok); FAQ numbers 0.018/0.032/0.055/$18/$3.40/$1.20 match suggestedStoryKit/ProfileKit (ok). Not backed: llms.txt links all point to the retired duncan-haywood.github.io host; sitemap.xml uses relative <loc> values (invalid per sitemaps.org) and robots.txt Sitemap line is relative; no canonical link on index.html. README 'After using this, you can now send...' benefit claim is untested (VENTURE.yaml: all hypotheses untested, stage prototype). Starting rates labelled 'ballpark, not industry standard' honestly.
evidence.fitness: Walked a shop job: pick 2-story colonial preset, enter footage, set wages, get price $6,782 and walk-away $4,612, copy summary and build a proposal. Works end to end. But the wage is one hourly figure applied to 'crew-hours' with no crew-size input, so a two- or three-person crew (the norm for installs) must be hand-converted or the labor is understated; the default 140 ft ranch prices at $12.49/ft against the $4.50 special the page tells shops to compare to, with a placeholder of $630, so the first walk-through shows a number the shop will distrust unless it adjusts rates. No material waste/overlap factor, no sales tax, no seamless-machine/truck cost per job beyond one flat travel number.
evidence.domain: Compared with the standard estimating practice: cost build-up then margin on price is sound and matches contractor guidance. Departures: no crew-size/man-hour distinction; no waste allowance on trough, hangers or downspouts (typical 5-10 percent); hanger spacing, end caps, sealant, screws and flashing are absent as material lines; hours per foot are unsourced (README admits). Overhead 16 percent plus 32 percent net margin on top is a high stack that explains the $12/ft output versus common published installed ranges, which I could not retrieve to cite. A working estimator would adjust several defaults in the first hour.

defects.what: No crew-size input: one hourly wage times 'crew-hours', so multi-person crews are undercosted unless the user pre-multiplies the wage; the page does not say so.
No material waste, end-cap, sealant, screw or flashing lines; hangers only as an optional upgrade.

Default ranch preset prices at about $12.49/ft versus the $4.50/ft special it is framed against and the $630 input placeholder; defaults are unsourced and may read as unrealistic to a first-time shop.
llms.txt links point at the retired duncan-haywood.github.io host, not marisstella.app.
sitemap.xml and robots.txt Sitemap line use relative URLs, which crawlers ignore; no canonical link on index.html.
flag() treats any unrecognised string (e.g. 'no') as true.
README omits shipped proposal, terms and share features.

verdict: The arithmetic is right (three presets recomputed independently to the cent, page figures match) and the 122 tests catch two seeded mutations, so correctness and verification meet the bar, and the feature set is finished as described. It falls short of the senior-estimator bar on fitness and domain: no crew-size handling, no waste or small-parts materials, unsourced hour and cost defaults that put the headline example at about $12.49/ft, and a VENTURE.yaml that still records every hypothesis as untested. Claims lose a point for the stale llms.txt host and invalid sitemap. By the computed rule claims is 2, so it does not meet the bar, but it is finished.
